text:
The suspect should be found not guilty if the arrest was lawful and the jury believes his account, because a punch used only to stop an unprovoked nightstick beating is reasonable self-defense against excessive force, which the statute does not forbid. He is guilty if the jury believes the officer, since that account has him striking first to resist a known arrest. Whether the arrest itself was lawful does not decide guilt once the statute has removed any right to resist.

CONFIDENCE: 78
